slides.title: Calming Robot Pitches? Exploring the Influence of Robot Voice Pitch on Children's Stress Levels
slides.tldr: ROBOT VOICE PITCH AND CHILD STRESS
slides.highlight: This study investigates how robot speech pitch affects stress levels in children during a timed task, providing insights for the design of social robots in RwB.

card.one_liner: Lower-pitched robot voices do not significantly reduce stress levels in children during a timed task.
card.key_idea: The study manipulated a Zenbo Junior II robot's voice pitch (±35 Hz) to test if human-like calming effects of lower pitch generalize to synthetic voices in child-robot interactions.
card.evaluation: 27 children (8-12 years) performed a timed LEGO task; stress was measured via adapted CAM-S questionnaires. Results showed no statistically significant difference between pitch conditions.
card.limitation: Relied solely on self-report measures; low-stakes task design and robot novelty may have suppressed overall stress levels.

slides.authors: Nina G. M. van Roij et al.

slides.title: Galaxy General Unveils Self-Learning Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: The introduction of a self-learning humanoid robot reflects an inflection point in embodied AI, providing insights relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: RoboColiseum Launches Standardized Simulation Platform for Embodied AI Evaluation
slides.tldr: STANDARDIZED SIMULATION PLATFORM FOR EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: The launch of a standardized simulation platform for embodied AI evaluation is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

slides.title: Humanoid Musical Robots as Experimental Interfaces for Music-Evoked Emotion
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOTS FOR MUSIC-EVOKED EMOTION RESEARCH
slides.highlight: This paper proposes using musical humanoid robots as interfaces to study music-evoked emotions through the control of acoustic and non-acoustic variables, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposes using humanoid musical robots as experimental interfaces to study multimodal, embodied music-evoked emotions.
card.key_idea: Humanoid robots enable parametric control, reproducibility, and decoupling of acoustic and visual variables, allowing researchers to isolate specific mechanisms of emotion induction like contagion and entrainment.
card.evaluation: Technical feasibility was demonstrated via the WAS-5 saxophonist robot, showing reproducible sound pressure control and successful closed-loop behavioral synchronization (feet-tapping) with participants.
card.limitation: Constrained by current robotic hardware, potential uncanny valley effects, and cultural variability in human receptivity toward robots.

slides.authors: Vincent K. M. Cheung et al.

slides.title: Real-TurnTurk: A Multimodal Turkish Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal Turkish corpus of unscripted dyadic interactions to model turn-taking dynamics, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Introduces Real-TurnTurk, a multimodal Turkish corpus for predicting turn-taking transitions in natural dyadic conversations.
card.key_idea: Uses a Genetic Algorithm to optimize interpretable AND-OR decision rules based on 28 visual, acoustic, and linguistic features extracted from a 2-second window.
card.evaluation: 5-fold conversation-level cross-validation against silence and random baselines; achieved F1=57.0%, showing modest improvement over the always-positive baseline (F1=50.0%).
card.limitation: Small dataset (11 conversations) with speaker imbalance and lack of listener-side visual cues (e.g., gaze, nodding).

slides.title: Counterfactual, Per-Decision Bias Auditing for Automated Hiring: Localizing and Explaining Disparate Impact in Applicant Tracking Systems
slides.tldr: PER-DECISION BIAS AUDITING FOR AUTOMATED HIRING
slides.highlight: The AI Bias Firewall (AIBF) provides a method to localize and explain disparate impact in automated systems through per-decision counterfactual shifts. This is relevant to MIMIC for analyzing the impact of AI-driven decision-making on societal-scale fairness and human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: AIBF audits automated hiring by using counterfactual shifts to localize and explain individual biased decisions.
card.key_idea: Neutralizes protected-attribute proxies to a privileged baseline, re-scores candidates, and measures the counterfactual shift to flag outcome-changing bias and provide additive explanations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Adult and COMPAS datasets; achieved 0.963 AUC for flip detection and surfaced 55% of harmed candidates by reviewing only 5% of decisions.
card.limitation: Correcting flagged decisions doesn't reach full legal parity because merit features often carry residual proxy correlations.

slides.title: Towards Actionable Surgical Team Dynamics: from Teamwork to Counterfactual Annotations
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal dataset featuring speaker diarization and interaction annotations, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on diarization and the perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: An extended multimodal surgical dataset featuring multi-level teamwork annotations and counterfactuals to analyze team performance degradation.
card.key_idea: Enriches the MM-OR dataset with speaker diarization, bilingual transcripts, and a hierarchical annotation framework (team, interaction, and individual levels) plus counterfactual breakdown triggers.
card.evaluation: 169 samples reviewed by three annotators using standardized protocols (OTAS, HMT, NOTSS, BFTQ, SYMLOG, GLIS); results show moderate class imbalance toward positive performance.
card.limitation: The dataset is based on a medical-grade phantom rather than real patients, potentially affecting the ecological validity of interaction dynamics.

slides.authors: Vincenzo Marco De Luca et al.

slides.title: Dual-Scale State-Space Modeling with Speaker-Wise Dynamic CRF for Speech Emotion Recognition in Conversation
slides.highlight: This work proposes DSSM-CRF to model emotion evolution and cross-speaker influence in conversations, contributing to HyECHO's goals of multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: DSSM-CRF improves conversational speech emotion recognition by separating cross-speaker context from within-speaker emotion evolution.
card.key_idea: Dual-scale bidirectional state-space models encode frame and dialogue context, while a speaker-wise dynamic CRF decodes independent emotion chains using global priors and pair-conditioned transition residuals.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on IEMOCAP and MELD against multiple baselines. Results (e.g., 75.81% UA on IEMOCAP) are supported by component ablations and backbone robustness tests.
card.limitation: Abrupt within-speaker emotion changes (shifts) remain significantly harder to predict than emotion persistence (inertia).

slides.title: LLM-Based Selection of Incongruent Verbal and Nonverbal Behavior for Virtual Humans
slides.highlight: This research explores using LLMs to select mismatched verbal and nonverbal behaviors based on social context, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: LLMs can generate realistic virtual humans by selecting nonverbal behaviors that contradict verbal content based on context.
card.key_idea: A taxonomy of verbal-nonverbal mismatches (e.g., irony, deception) used to test three prompting levels (utterance, dialogue, and context) for selecting Action Units and gaze shifts.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via Claude-3.5-Sonnet output analysis and two human-subject studies (N=49 and N=39) using video stimuli and Likert scales; results were statistically significant.
card.limitation: Lacks integration of body gestures, postural shifts, and voice prosody; requires manual mapping of LLM descriptions to animation parameters.

slides.title: Collective Counterfactual Planning: Coordination, Consent, and Verification under Representational Constraints
slides.tldr: FORMAL MODEL FOR COLLECTIVE PLANNING UNDER REPRESENTATIONAL CONSTRAINTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces Collective Counterfactual Planning to model how agents with limited representational subspaces coordinate to achieve goals, supporting MIMIC's focus on agent models in hybrid societies.

card.one_liner: A formal model of collective planning where agent limitations are defined by representational subspace geometry.
card.key_idea: Agents perceive and act via orthogonal projections. Solvability depends on four gates: exogenous implementation, representational conception, consent (memoryless or audited), and verification qualification.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via machine-checked geometric examples (E1, E2) and theorems proving the duality of collective reach and blindness.
card.limitation: The model is non-strategic, assuming truthful agents who share goals and consent mechanically without incentives or deception.

slides.title: Mitigating Speaker Leakage in Cascaded Multi-talker ASR with Diarization-based Transcript Correction
slides.tldr: REDUCING SPEAKER LEAKAGE IN MULTI-TALKER ASR
slides.highlight: This work proposes a pruning-based paradigm using speaker diarization to remove leakage artifacts in multi-talker ASR, supporting HyECHO's focus on diarization and social perception.

card.one_liner: A pruning-based algorithm that reduces speaker leakage in cascaded multi-talker ASR using diarization-based verification.
card.key_idea: Prunes transcribed words based on a tripartite consensus of acoustic containment (diarization windows), lexical cross-validation, and temporal alignment between parallel speaker transcripts.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on LibriMix, LibriSpeechMix, and AMI corpus using cpWER; showed relative reductions up to 29% in high-leakage scenarios.
card.limitation: An experimental joint separation-diarization architecture proved highly sensitive to acoustic domain shifts and SNR of training data.

slides.title: Why Personalization Matters: Cross-Subject Challenges in EMG-IMU-based HRI Activity Recognition
slides.highlight: This research introduces the MAGIC-HRI dataset for recognizing gestures and activities in human-robot interaction, demonstrating that personalization is necessary to overcome subject dependence. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Personalization is essential for robust EMG-IMU activity recognition in HRI due to high inter-subject variability.
card.key_idea: Introduces MAGIC-HRI dataset (53 classes) and evaluates Random Forest classifiers using a Leave-One-Subject-Out protocol, demonstrating that injecting few user-specific samples significantly improves recognition accuracy.
card.evaluation: Tested 11 subjects using Random Forest and other classifiers. LOSO protocol revealed a large generalization gap compared to 75/25 splits.
card.limitation: Lacks robot-in-the-loop evaluation in online settings and shows poor initial generalization to unseen subjects without personalization.

slides.authors: Ruan Rithelle Chagas de Faria Carminati et al.

slides.title: GenCoord: Skill-Path Commitments under Private Information
slides.highlight: GenCoord enables embodied agents to coordinate joint tasks by turning private information into executable skill-path commitments, improving success rates and reducing communication overhead. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied AI.

card.one_liner: GenCoord enables multi-agent coordination by treating executable skill-path commitments as the primary unit of communication.
card.key_idea: Agents use a local Qwen3.5-0.8B model to generate a multi-step SELF+REQ commitment object, resolved via forward requests or bounded feedback to handle private information.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in Minecraft using 128 held-out semantic clusters; compared against JSON and free-form communication via success rates, wire bytes, and time-to-commitment.
card.limitation: Performance drops to 0% on unseen transform-order motifs, indicating a reliance on familiar task-structure motifs.

slides.title: Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity for Real-Time Online Motor Learning in Physical Human--Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME ONLINE MOTOR LEARNING VIA FREE-ENERGY-GATED PLASTICITY
slides.highlight: This work introduces Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity (FEGP) to enable robots to acquire new motor patterns during physical interaction without forgetting previous behaviors. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied learning and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A mechanism for real-time robot motor learning that regulates synaptic plasticity using variational free energy.
card.key_idea: Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity (FEGP) scales the learning rate of a PV-RNN via a sigmoidal gate driven by model-environment mismatch (variational free energy).
card.evaluation: Tested on 10 teaching streams with 5 initializations per stream; measured repertoire coverage and retention via DTW-based trajectory classification.
